records.literal_gloss: And heard Pashhur son of Immer the priest, and he [was] overseer, chief, in [the] house of Yahweh, Jeremiah prophesying the words the these.

en.L: And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who [was] chief officer in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
en.B: Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was the chief officer in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
en.R: Pashhur son of Immer was a priest and the chief officer in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He heard Jeremiah giving this message from God.

es.L: Y oyó Pasur hijo de Imer, el sacerdote, que [era] jefe supremo en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a Jeremías profetizar estas palabras.
es.B: Pasur hijo de Imer, el sacerdote que era el oficial principal en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, oyó a Jeremías profetizar estas cosas.
es.R: Pasur hijo de Imer era sacerdote y el oficial principal del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Él oyó a Jeremías dar este mensaje de parte de Dios.

sw.L: Naye Pashuri mwana wa Imeri, kuhani, aliyekuwa msimamizi mkuu katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akamsikia Yeremia akitabiri maneno haya.
sw.B: Basi Pashuri mwana wa Imeri, kuhani, aliyekuwa msimamizi mkuu katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, alimsikia Yeremia akitabiri mambo haya.
sw.R: Pashuri mwana wa Imeri alikuwa kuhani na msimamizi mkuu katika hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Alimsikia Yeremia akitoa ujumbe huu kutoka kwa Mungu.

decisions.choice: chief officer: the priest in charge of order in the temple
decisions.reason: The two words together name an overseer at the head of others. 29:26 describes this office: the officer in the house of the LORD was to put any madman who acted as a prophet in the stocks. So Pashhur acts here by the authority of his post, not as a private enemy.

decisions.choice: these words: the message of 19:14-15, and the warning of 19:1-13 behind it
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had just come back from the valley of Ben-hinnom, stood in the court of the LORD's house and announced that disaster would come on Jerusalem and its towns (19:14-15). This chapter tells what that cost him.

decisions.choice: Pashhur son of Immer: a priest of the family of Immer
decisions.reason: Immer was one of the priestly families (1 Chronicles 24:14; Ezra 2:37). This Pashhur is a different man from Pashhur son of Malchiah, who appears in 21:1 and 38:1.

decisions.choice: giving this message from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "prophesying these words" as speaking a message from God and splits the long sentence in two.

decisions.choice: Pasur hijo de Imer
decisions.reason: The published Spanish forms of 1 Chronicles 9:12, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: Pashuri mwana wa Imeri
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili form of Pashhur in these books; Immer as "Imeri".

source.text: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה פַשְׁח֔וּר אֵ֖ת יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹת֜וֹ עַל־הַמַּהְפֶּ֗כֶת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּשַׁ֤עַר בִּנְיָמִן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck Pashhur Jeremiah the prophet, and put him on the stocks that [were] in [the] gate of Benjamin the upper, which [was] in [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that [were] in the upper Benjamin Gate, which [was] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Pashhur beat Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the upper Benjamin Gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Pashhur beat Jeremiah the prophet. Then he locked him in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y golpeó Pasur a Jeremías el profeta, y lo puso en el cepo que [estaba] en la puerta superior de Benjamín, que [estaba] en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pasur hizo azotar al profeta Jeremías y lo puso en el cepo que había en la puerta superior de Benjamín, en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Pasur golpeó al profeta Jeremías. Luego lo encerró en el cepo, en la puerta superior de Benjamín del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Naye Pashuri akampiga Yeremia nabii, akamtia katika mkatale uliokuwa katika Lango la juu la Benyamini, lililokuwa katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Pashuri alimpiga Yeremia nabii, akamtia katika mkatale kwenye Lango la juu la Benyamini la nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Pashuri alimpiga Yeremia nabii. Kisha akamfunga katika mkatale kwenye Lango la Juu la Benyamini la hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: struck: beat, probably a set number of blows as a punishment
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike. Used of an official punishment it can mean a beating with a rod or a flogging (Deuteronomy 25:2-3; compare 37:15, where officials beat Jeremiah again). The text does not say whether Pashhur struck him himself or had it done.

decisions.choice: the stocks: a frame that held the prisoner in a cramped, bent position
alternatives: a frame that held neck and hands
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to turn or twist, and seems to name a device that held the body bent and fixed. The seer Hanani was put in it by King Asa (2 Chronicles 16:10), and 29:26 names it as the punishment for a man who acts like a prophet. Its exact form is not known.

decisions.choice: the upper Benjamin Gate: a gate on the north side of the temple courts
decisions.reason: The Benjamin Gate of the city faced north toward the land of Benjamin (37:13; 38:7). This one is called "upper" and is said to be in the house of the LORD, so it was a gate of the temple area on that side, perhaps the upper gate that King Jotham built (2 Kings 15:35; compare Ezekiel 9:2). Jeremiah was put on public view where worshipers passed.

decisions.choice: in the stocks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "on" the stocks, since the prisoner was fastened to the frame; English says "in" the stocks. Readable says "locked" to show that he could not get out.

decisions.choice: el cepo
decisions.reason: The frame that held a prisoner bent and cramped (meaning decision m2); "cepo" is the Spanish word for such a wooden frame, used at every level.

decisions.choice: mkatale
decisions.reason: "Mkatale" is the wooden frame that held a prisoner's feet or body, which is what the stocks were; "pingu" are handcuffs.

records.literal_gloss: And it was on [the] next day, and brought out Pashhur Jeremiah from the stocks, and said to him Jeremiah: Not Pashhur has called Yahweh your name, but rather Magor-missabib.

en.L: And it happened on the next day that Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks. And Jeremiah said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not called your name Pashhur, but Magor-missabib.
en.B: The next day, when Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks, Jeremiah told him, "Pashhur is not the name {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you. His name for you is Terror on Every Side.
en.R: The next day Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then Jeremiah said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is not calling you Pashhur any longer. He is calling you Terror All Around.

es.L: Y sucedió al día siguiente que Pasur sacó a Jeremías del cepo. Y le dijo Jeremías: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no ha llamado tu nombre Pasur, sino Magor-misabib.
es.B: Al día siguiente, cuando Pasur sacó a Jeremías del cepo, Jeremías le dijo: «Pasur no es el nombre que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te da. El nombre que él te da es Terror por Todas Partes.
es.R: Al día siguiente, Pasur sacó a Jeremías del cepo. Entonces Jeremías le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ya no te llama Pasur. Ahora te llama Terror por Todos Lados.

sw.L: Ikawa siku iliyofuata, Pashuri akamtoa Yeremia katika mkatale. Naye Yeremia akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakukuita jina lako Pashuri, bali Magor-misabibu.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata, Pashuri alipomtoa Yeremia katika mkatale, Yeremia alimwambia, "Pashuri si jina ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakupa. Jina lake kwako ni Hofu Kila Upande.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata Pashuri alimtoa Yeremia katika mkatale. Ndipo Yeremia akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuiti tena Pashuri. Anakuita Hofu Pande Zote.

decisions.choice: Magor-missabib: a name that means "terror on every side"
decisions.reason: The new name is a phrase: "terror" and "from all around". When God gives a person a new name, the name declares what that person is or will become (Genesis 17:5; Hosea 1:4-9; Isaiah 8:3). Verse 4 explains it: Pashhur will become a terror to himself and to all his friends. The name of the man who put the prophet in the stocks becomes a sign of the disaster the prophet announced.

decisions.choice: terror on every side: one of Jeremiah's sayings
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 6:25; 20:10; 46:5; 49:29 and Lamentations 2:22 (compare Psalm 31:14). In verse 10 Jeremiah's enemies throw it back at him.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's words run from here to the end of verse 6
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks to Pashhur in verses 3-6. Within his words he gives a message from the LORD (verses 4-6), which is set inside his speech.

decisions.choice: Terror on Every Side / Terror All Around
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, Magor-missabib. Balanced and Readable give its meaning, because the point of the name is what it says; the wording matches 6:25 and verse 10 so the saying can be recognized. A footnote gives the Hebrew name.

decisions.choice: is not the name the LORD gives you (Balanced); is not calling you (Readable) ... His name for you is
decisions.reason: "Called your name" is the Hebrew way of saying "named you"; Balanced and Readable say it in ordinary English.

decisions.choice: Terror por Todas Partes (Balanced); Terror por Todos Lados (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name; Balanced and Readable translate it so that its meaning, "terror on every side" (meaning decision m1), is heard. The same Spanish words return for the saying in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Hofu Kila Upande (Balanced); Hofu Pande Zote (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable translate the new name so its meaning is heard, as the English does; Literal keeps the Hebrew name in Swahili spelling.

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה הִנְנִי֩ נֹתֶנְךָ֨לְמָג֜וֹר לְךָ֣ וּלְכָל־אֹהֲבֶ֗יךָ וְנָֽפְל֛וּ בְּחֶ֥רֶב אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם וְעֵינֶ֣יךָ רֹא֑וֹת וְאֶת־כָּל־יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶתֵּן֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְהִגְלָ֥ם בָּבֶ֖לָה וְהִכָּ֥ם בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Behold I [am] making you into a terror to yourself and to all your friends, and they will fall by [the] sword of their enemies, and your eyes [will be] seeing; and all Judah I will give into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he will exile them to Babylon and strike them with the sword.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'See, I am making you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. And they will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. And all Judah I will give into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will carry them into exile to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'I am about to turn you into a terror to yourself and to everyone who loves you. Before your own eyes they will fall by the swords of their enemies. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon. He will carry them away to Babylon as exiles and put them to the sword.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'I will turn you into a terror, both to yourself and to all your friends. You will watch as your friends are killed by their enemies' swords. I will hand all the people of Judah over to the king of Babylon. He will take them away to Babylon as prisoners and kill them with the sword.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “He aquí, yo te convierto en terror para ti mismo y para todos tus amigos. Y ellos caerán por la espada de sus enemigos, y tus ojos lo verán. Y a todo Judá entregaré en mano del rey de Babilonia, y él los llevará cautivos a Babilonia y los herirá a espada.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: “Voy a convertirte en un terror para ti mismo y para todos los que te aman. Ante tus propios ojos caerán por la espada de sus enemigos. Entregaré a todo Judá en manos del rey de Babilonia. Él los llevará cautivos a Babilonia y los pasará a espada.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Haré que seas un terror para ti mismo y para todos tus amigos. Verás cómo sus enemigos matan a espada a tus amigos. Entregaré a toda la gente de Judá en manos del rey de Babilonia. Él se los llevará presos a Babilonia y los matará a espada.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: 'Tazama, ninakufanya kuwa kitisho kwako mwenyewe na kwa rafiki zako wote. Nao wataanguka kwa upanga wa adui zao huku macho yako yakitazama. Na Yuda yote nitaitia mkononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atawachukua mateka mpaka Babeli, na kuwapiga kwa upanga.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: 'Ninakaribia kukufanya kuwa kitisho kwako mwenyewe na kwa wote wanaokupenda. Wataanguka kwa panga za adui zao mbele ya macho yako. Nitaitia Yuda yote mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli. Atawachukua mateka mpaka Babeli na kuwaua kwa upanga.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: 'Nitakufanya kuwa kitisho, kwako mwenyewe na kwa rafiki zako wote. Utaona rafiki zako wakiuawa kwa panga za adui zao. Nitawatia watu wote wa Yuda mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli. Atawachukua mpaka Babeli kama wafungwa na kuwaua kwa upanga.

decisions.choice: a terror to yourself and to all your friends: the meaning of the new name
decisions.reason: "Terror" is the first word of the name in verse 3. Pashhur will live in dread, and he will be a cause of dread to the people around him, because he will see them die and know that he told them all would be well (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon: the first time Jeremiah names the enemy
decisions.reason: Until now the book has spoken of a disaster and a people coming from the north without naming them (1:14-15; 4:6; 6:1, 22). Here Babylon is named for the first time as the power to which God will hand Judah over, and from here on it is named often (21:2-10; 25:9-11).

decisions.choice: your eyes seeing: Pashhur will watch it happen
decisions.reason: The words are a short clause of circumstance: the friends fall while Pashhur looks on. He is not killed with them but lives to go into exile (verse 6).

decisions.choice: carry into exile ... strike with the sword: two fates for the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe what the king will do to Judah as a whole: some are taken away and others killed. The text does not divide them further.

decisions.choice: See, I am making (Literal); I am about to turn you into (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens with a word that calls for attention, followed by a form that means something is about to happen. Literal gives the call to attention as "See" rather than the older "behold"; Balanced shows the nearness with "about to"; Readable says simply "I will". Balanced gives "your friends" as "everyone who loves you", which is what the Hebrew word says.

decisions.choice: You will watch as your friends are killed ... all the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are and turns "fall by the sword" into plain words; "all Judah" means the people of the land.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֗י אֶת־כָּל־חֹ֨סֶן֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶת־כָּל־יְגִיעָ֖הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־יְקָרָ֑הּ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אוֹצְר֜וֹת מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶתֵּן֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְזָזוּם֙ וּלְקָח֔וּם וֶהֱבִיא֖וּם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give all [the] stored wealth of the city the this and all its labor and all its precious [things]; and all [the] treasures of [the] kings of Judah I will give into [the] hand of their enemies, and they will plunder them and take them and bring them to Babylon.

en.L: And I will give all the stored wealth of this city, and all its gain, and all its precious things; and all the treasures of the kings of Judah I will give into the hand of their enemies, and they will plunder them and take them and bring them to Babylon.
en.B: I will hand over to their enemies all the wealth stored up in this city, all that its people have worked for, all its valuable things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will loot them, seize them and haul them away to Babylon.
en.R: I will let their enemies take all the riches stored in this city, everything the people worked to get, and all their valuable things. Their enemies will also take all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will grab it all and carry it away to Babylon.

es.L: Y entregaré toda la riqueza guardada de esta ciudad, y todo su fruto del trabajo, y todas sus cosas preciosas; y todos los tesoros de los reyes de Judá entregaré en mano de sus enemigos, y los saquearán, y los tomarán, y los llevarán a Babilonia.
es.B: Entregaré a sus enemigos toda la riqueza acumulada en esta ciudad, todo lo que su gente ha ganado con su trabajo, todos sus objetos de valor y todos los tesoros de los reyes de Judá. Los saquearán, se los llevarán y los trasladarán a Babilonia.
es.R: Dejaré que sus enemigos se lleven todas las riquezas guardadas en esta ciudad, todo lo que la gente ganó con su trabajo y todas sus cosas de valor. Sus enemigos también se llevarán todos los tesoros de los reyes de Judá. Lo agarrarán todo y se lo llevarán a Babilonia.

sw.L: Nami nitatoa mali yote iliyowekwa akiba ya mji huu, na mapato yake yote, na vitu vyake vyote vya thamani; na hazina zote za wafalme wa Yuda nitazitia mkononi mwa adui zao, nao watazitwaa nyara, na kuzichukua, na kuzipeleka Babeli.
sw.B: Nitawapa adui zao mali yote iliyohifadhiwa katika mji huu, yote ambayo watu wake wameyafanyia kazi, vitu vyake vyote vya thamani, na hazina zote za wafalme wa Yuda. Watazipora, watazinyakua na kuzipeleka Babeli.
sw.R: Nitawaacha adui zao wachukue utajiri wote uliohifadhiwa katika mji huu, kila kitu watu walichofanya kazi kukipata, na vitu vyao vyote vya thamani. Adui zao watachukua pia hazina zote za wafalme wa Yuda. Watanyakua vyote na kuvipeleka Babeli.

decisions.choice: stored wealth ... labor ... precious things: three words for everything of value
decisions.reason: The first word means wealth laid up in store, the second what has been gained by hard work, the third things prized for their value. Together with the kings' treasures they cover all that the city owns.

decisions.choice: the treasures of the kings of Judah carried to Babylon
decisions.reason: Isaiah had said the same to King Hezekiah (Isaiah 39:6; 2 Kings 20:17). 2 Kings 24:13 and 25:13-17 tell how the king of Babylon took the treasures of the palace and the temple.

decisions.choice: them: the riches and treasures
decisions.reason: The three verbs at the end have the goods as their object, not the people: the enemies plunder the wealth, take it and bring it to Babylon.

decisions.choice: one list, then one verb
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I will give" twice, before and after the list. Balanced gathers the list under one verb, which English handles better; Literal keeps both.

decisions.choice: grab it all and carry it away
decisions.reason: Readable says "it all" so it is clear that the goods, not the people, are taken.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה פַשְׁח֗וּר וְכֹל֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵיתֶ֔ךָ תֵּלְכ֖וּ בַּשֶּׁ֑בִי וּבָבֶ֣ל תָּב֗וֹא וְשָׁ֤ם תָּמוּת֙ וְשָׁ֣ם תִּקָּבֵ֔ר אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־אֹ֣הֲבֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נִבֵּ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם בַּשָּֽׁקֶר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, Pashhur, and all dwellers of your house, you will go into captivity; and Babylon you will enter, and there you will die and there you will be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied to them in falsehood.

en.L: And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house will go into captivity. And to Babylon you will come, and there you will die, and there you will be buried, you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely.'"
en.B: As for you, Pashhur, you and everyone in your household will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and you will die and be buried there, together with all the friends to whom you have prophesied lies.'"
en.R: And you, Pashhur, and everyone who lives in your house will be taken away as prisoners. You will go to Babylon. You will die there and be buried there. So will all your friends, the people you told lies to when you prophesied.'"

es.L: Y tú, Pasur, y todos los que habitan en tu casa irán al cautiverio. Y a Babilonia llegarás, y allí morirás, y allí serás sepultado, tú y todos tus amigos a quienes has profetizado con mentira”».
es.B: En cuanto a ti, Pasur, tú y todos los de tu casa irán al cautiverio. Irás a Babilonia, y allí morirás y serás sepultado, junto con todos los amigos a quienes les has profetizado mentiras”».
es.R: Y tú, Pasur, y todos los que viven en tu casa serán llevados presos. Irás a Babilonia. Allí morirás y allí te enterrarán. Lo mismo les pasará a todos tus amigos, la gente a la que le dijiste mentiras cuando profetizabas”».

sw.L: Nawe, Pashuri, na wote wakaao nyumbani mwako mtakwenda utumwani. Nawe utafika Babeli, na huko utakufa, na huko utazikwa, wewe na rafiki zako wote uliowatabiria kwa uongo.'"
sw.B: Na wewe, Pashuri, wewe pamoja na wote wa nyumbani mwako mtakwenda utumwani. Utakwenda Babeli, nawe utafia huko na kuzikwa huko, pamoja na rafiki zako wote uliowatabiria uongo.'"
sw.R: Nawe Pashuri, pamoja na wote wanaoishi nyumbani mwako, mtachukuliwa kama wafungwa. Utakwenda Babeli. Utafia huko na kuzikwa huko. Ndivyo itakavyokuwa pia kwa rafiki zako wote, wale uliowaambia uongo ulipotabiri.'"

decisions.choice: you have prophesied falsely: Pashhur also spoke as a prophet, and his message was a lie
decisions.reason: Pashhur was a priest, yet he too gave messages in God's name, no doubt that the city was safe (compare 14:13-15; 23:16-17). Jeremiah calls this "falsehood", the word the book uses for lying prophecy (5:31; 14:14; 27:10).

decisions.choice: die and be buried in a foreign land
decisions.reason: To die and be buried away from the land of Israel was a mark of judgment (22:11-12, 26). The prophet Amos had told the priest Amaziah, who tried to silence him, that he would die in an unclean land (Amos 7:17).

decisions.choice: you will go: first plural, then singular
decisions.reason: The first verb is plural, for Pashhur and his household together; the next ones are singular and turn to Pashhur himself, and the verse ends by adding his friends.

decisions.choice: falsely / lies
decisions.reason: Literal "falsely" and Balanced "lies" both give the word for falsehood. The verse ends the LORD's message and Jeremiah's words, so both quotations close here.

decisions.choice: con mentira (Literal); mentiras (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Sheqer* is "mentira" through the block, as the terms note sets for Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: kwa uongo / uongo
decisions.reason: *Sheqer* is "uongo" throughout this block.

source.text: פִּתִּיתַ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וָֽאֶפָּ֔ת חֲזַקְתַּ֖נִי וַתּוּכָ֑ל הָיִ֤יתִי לִשְׂחוֹק֙ כָּל־הַיּ֔וֹם כֻּלֹּ֖ה לֹעֵ֥ג לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You enticed me, Yahweh, and I was enticed; you were stronger than me and you prevailed; I have become a laughingstock all the day; all of him mocks me.

en.L: You enticed me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I was enticed; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were stronger than I, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} prevailed. \q I have become a laughingstock all the day; \q all of them mock me.
en.B: You enticed me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I was taken in; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were too strong for me, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} won. \q All day long people laugh at me; \q every one of them makes fun of me.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} lured me in, and I was fooled. \q You were stronger than I was, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} won. \q People laugh at me all day long. \q Everyone makes fun of me.

es.L: Me sedujiste, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y fui seducido; \q más fuerte fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que yo, y prevaleciste. \q He sido objeto de risa todo el día; \q todos ellos se burlan de mí.
es.B: Me sedujiste, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y me dejé seducir; \q fuiste demasiado fuerte para mí, y me venciste. \q Todo el día se ríen de mí; \q cada uno de ellos se burla de mí.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me atrajiste, y yo me dejé engañar. \q Eras más fuerte que yo, y me venciste. \q La gente se ríe de mí todo el día. \q Todos se burlan de mí.

sw.L: Umenishawishi, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami nikashawishika; \q ulikuwa na nguvu kuliko mimi, nawe ukashinda. \q Nimekuwa kichekesho mchana kutwa; \q kila mmoja ananidhihaki.
sw.B: Umenishawishi, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami nikadanganyika; \q ulinizidi nguvu, nawe ukashinda. \q Mchana kutwa watu hunicheka; \q kila mmoja wao hunidhihaki.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ulinivuta, nami nikadanganyika. \q Ulikuwa na nguvu kuliko mimi, nawe ukashinda. \q Watu hunicheka mchana kutwa. \q Kila mtu hunidhihaki.

decisions.choice: the start of Jeremiah's fifth lament: his prayer to God about what his calling has cost him
decisions.reason: Verses 7-18 are the last of Jeremiah's prayers of complaint (11:18-12:6; 15:10-21; 17:14-18; 18:18-23). Coming straight after the night in the stocks, it moves from accusation (verses 7-10) to trust (verses 11-13) and then to the bitterest words in the book (verses 14-18). Unlike 12:5-6 and 15:19-21, no answer from God follows.

decisions.choice: you enticed me: God drew Jeremiah into his task by a persuasion he could not resist, and he now feels deceived
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade someone by working on them until they give in. It is used of seducing a young woman (Exodus 22:15), of luring someone into a trap (Judges 14:15; 16:5), of the spirit sent to deceive King Ahab (1 Kings 22:20-22), and of gentle persuasion (Proverbs 25:15). Jeremiah had been promised that God would be with him (1:8, 19); now, beaten and mocked, he says he was talked into more than he knew. Whether he accuses God of deceit or of a persuasion too strong to refuse cannot be settled; the word carries both.

decisions.choice: you were stronger than I, and you prevailed: God overpowered his resistance
decisions.reason: The first verb means to be strong or to take hold of by force; the second to be able, to win. Jeremiah did not want the task (1:6), but God was the stronger. The same pair of ideas returns in verse 10, where his enemies hope that he will be enticed and that they will prevail, and in verse 11, where they will not prevail.

decisions.choice: all of him: everyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "all of it" or "all of him", meaning the whole crowd, every one of them.

decisions.choice: enticed (Literal, Balanced); lured ... fooled (Readable)
decisions.reason: The choice keeps the sense of being drawn in by persuasion, with the hint of being deceived that the verb carries, rather than the flat "deceived" or the sexual "seduced". Balanced and Readable give the passive verb as "taken in" and "fooled". The same English words are used for the same verb in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Me sedujiste ... fui seducido (Literal, Balanced); me atrajiste ... me dejé engañar (Readable)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's word for how God drew him in (meaning decision m2) keeps "seducir" at Literal and Balanced, which carries both persuasion and the sense of being taken in; Readable says it plainly. Verse 10 repeats the same verb.

decisions.choice: umenishawishi ... nikashawishika (Literal); umenishawishi ... nikadanganyika (Balanced); ulinivuta ... nikadanganyika (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Kushawishi" is to persuade or entice; Literal repeats the verb as the Hebrew does, Balanced and Readable say how Jeremiah felt taken in. The lament is Jeremiah's own prayer, set in lines.

source.text: כִּֽי־מִדֵּ֤י אֲדַבֵּר֙ אֶזְעָ֔ק חָמָ֥ס וָשֹׁ֖ד אֶקְרָ֑א כִּֽי־הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֥ה לִ֛י לְחֶרְפָּ֥ה וּלְקֶ֖לֶס כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: For as often as I speak, I cry out; violence and destruction I proclaim; for has become [the] word of Yahweh to me for reproach and for derision all the day.

en.L: For as often as I speak, I cry out; \q "Violence and destruction!" I proclaim. \q For the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has become to me a reproach and a derision all the day.
en.B: Whenever I speak, I cry out; \q I shout, "Violence and ruin!" \q So the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought me insult and scorn all day long.
en.R: Every time I speak, I cry out. \q I shout, "Violence! Destruction!" \q Because of the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, people insult me and laugh at me all day long.

es.L: Porque cada vez que hablo, grito; \q «¡Violencia y destrucción!», proclamo. \q Porque la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se me ha vuelto oprobio y escarnio todo el día.
es.B: Cada vez que hablo, tengo que gritar; \q clamo: «¡Violencia y ruina!». \q Así, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} me ha traído insultos y burlas todo el día.
es.R: Cada vez que hablo, grito. \q Grito: «¡Violencia! ¡Destrucción!». \q Por el mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, la gente me insulta y se ríe de mí todo el día.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila ninaposema, ninalia; \q "Udhalimu na uharibifu!" ninatangaza. \q Kwa maana neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} limekuwa kwangu aibu na dhihaka mchana kutwa.
sw.B: Kila ninaposema, ninalia kwa sauti; \q ninapiga kelele, "Udhalimu na maangamizi!" \q Kwa hiyo neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} limeniletea matusi na dharau mchana kutwa.
sw.R: Kila mara ninaposema, ninalia kwa sauti. \q Ninapiga kelele, "Udhalimu! Maangamizi!" \q Kwa sababu ya ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, watu hunitukana na kunicheka mchana kutwa.

decisions.choice: violence and destruction: the disaster he must announce
alternatives: his own cry for help: "I am being wronged!"
decisions.reason: These two words sum up the message God gave Jeremiah: violence and ruin are coming on the city (6:7). They could also be his cry for help as one who suffers violence (compare Job 19:7; Habakkuk 1:2-3), but the next line, which says the word of the LORD is what brings him scorn, points to the content of his message.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the mockery of verse 7
decisions.reason: The second "for" explains why he is a laughingstock: the message God gave him is one of disaster, so speaking it brings him nothing but insult.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "So" for the second "for", since in English the line reads as the result of what he has to say.

decisions.choice: people insult me and laugh at me
decisions.reason: Readable says who does the insulting, turning "reproach and derision" into plain verbs.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לֹֽא־אֶזְכְּרֶ֗נּוּ וְלֹֽא־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עוֹד֙ בִּשְׁמ֔וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה בְלִבִּי֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ בֹּעֶ֔רֶת עָצֻ֖ר בְּעַצְמֹתָ֑י וְנִלְאֵ֥יתִי כַּֽלְכֵ֖ל וְלֹ֥א אוּכָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [if] I say, Not I will remember him and not I will speak again in his name, then it is in my heart like a fire burning, shut up in my bones; and I am weary of holding [it] in, and not I am able.

en.L: And [if] I say, "I will not remember {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or speak again in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name," \q then it is in my heart like a burning fire, \q shut up in my bones; \q and I am weary of holding [it] in, and I cannot.
en.B: If I say, "I will not mention {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or speak in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name anymore," \q then it is like a fire burning in my heart, \q shut up inside my bones. \q I wear myself out holding it in, and I cannot.
en.R: If I say, "I will not mention {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I will not speak in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name anymore," \q then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message burns inside me like a fire, \q a fire trapped in my bones. \q I get tired of trying to hold it in. I cannot do it.

es.L: Y [si] digo: «No me acordaré de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ni hablaré más en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre», \q entonces está en mi corazón como un fuego ardiente \q encerrado en mis huesos; \q y me canso de contener[lo], y no puedo.
es.B: Si digo: «No lo mencionaré más ni hablaré más en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre», \q entonces es como un fuego que arde en mi corazón, \q encerrado dentro de mis huesos. \q Me agoto tratando de contenerlo, y no puedo.
es.R: Si digo: «No voy a hablar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Ya no hablaré en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre», \q entonces {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mensaje me quema por dentro como un fuego, \q un fuego encerrado en mis huesos. \q Me canso de tratar de aguantarlo. No puedo.

sw.L: Na [nikisema], "Sitamkumbuka {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, wala sitanena tena kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}," \q basi ndani ya moyo wangu [huwa] kama moto uwakao, \q uliofungwa ndani ya mifupa yangu; \q nami nimechoka kuuzuia, wala siwezi.
sw.B: Nikisema, "Sitamtaja wala sitasema tena kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}," \q basi huwa kama moto unaowaka moyoni mwangu, \q umefungiwa ndani ya mifupa yangu. \q Ninajichosha kuuzuia, nami siwezi.
sw.R: Nikisema, "Sitamtaja tena. Sitasema tena kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}," \q basi ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} huwaka ndani yangu kama moto, \q moto uliofungiwa ndani ya mifupa yangu. \q Ninachoka kujaribu kuuzuia. Siwezi.

decisions.choice: it: the word of the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject named. It is the word of the LORD from verse 8, which Jeremiah tries to keep to himself.

decisions.choice: a burning fire shut up in my bones: a pressure from within that cannot be held back
decisions.reason: The bones stand for the whole inner person. God had said his words in Jeremiah's mouth would be a fire (5:14; compare 23:29). Here the fire burns inside the prophet, and silence only makes it worse (compare Psalm 39:4).

decisions.choice: remember him: mention him, speak of him
decisions.reason: To remember someone in speech is to name or mention them (Exodus 23:13; Amos 6:10). Jeremiah means he will no longer speak for God.

decisions.choice: I cannot: the same verb as "prevailed" in verse 7
decisions.reason: "I am not able" uses the verb with which Jeremiah said God "prevailed" over him (verse 7). He cannot win against the word inside him any more than against God.

decisions.choice: his message burns inside me
decisions.reason: Readable names "it" as God's message (m1), since the plain subject would be unclear.

source.text: כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֜עְתִּי דִּבַּ֣ת רַבִּים֮ מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ הַגִּ֨ידוּ֙ וְנַגִּידֶ֔נּוּ כֹּ֚ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ שְׁלוֹמִ֔י שֹׁמְרֵ֖י צַלְעִ֑י אוּלַ֤י יְפֻתֶּה֙ וְנ֣וּכְלָה ל֔וֹ וְנִקְחָ֥ה נִקְמָתֵ֖נוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For I have heard [the] whispering of many: Terror from all around! Tell, and let us tell [on] him! All [the] men of my peace [are] watching [for] my stumbling: Perhaps he will be enticed, and we will prevail against him and take our vengeance on him.

en.L: For I have heard the whispering of many: "Terror on every side! \q Report [him], and let us report him!" \q All the men of my peace \q are watching for my stumbling: \q "Perhaps he will be enticed, and we will prevail against him \q and take our vengeance on him."
en.B: I hear many whispering, "Terror on every side! \q Inform on him! Let us inform on him!" \q All my trusted friends \q watch for me to stumble: \q "Perhaps he can be enticed; then we will get the better of him \q and take our revenge on him."
en.R: I hear many people whispering, "Terror all around! \q Report him! Let us report him!" \q Even my closest friends \q are waiting for me to slip. \q They say, "Maybe he can be fooled. Then we will beat him \q and pay him back."

es.L: Porque he oído la murmuración de muchos: «¡Terror por todas partes! \q ¡{{plural_you:Denuncien|Denunciad}}[lo], y lo denunciaremos!». \q Todos los hombres de mi paz \q acechan mi tropiezo: \q «Quizás será seducido, y prevaleceremos contra él \q y tomaremos de él nuestra venganza».
es.B: Oigo a muchos que murmuran: «¡Terror por todas partes! \q ¡{{plural_you:Denúncienlo|Denunciadlo}}! ¡Vamos a denunciarlo!». \q Todos mis amigos de confianza \q esperan que yo tropiece: \q «Quizás se le pueda seducir; entonces lo venceremos \q y nos vengaremos de él».
es.R: Oigo a mucha gente que murmura: «¡Hay terror por todos lados! \q ¡{{plural_you:Denúncienlo|Denunciadlo}}! ¡Vamos a denunciarlo!». \q Hasta mis amigos más cercanos \q esperan que yo dé un paso en falso. \q Dicen: «Quizás se le pueda engañar. Entonces lo venceremos \q y nos vengaremos de él».

sw.L: Kwa maana nimesikia minong'ono ya wengi: "Hofu kila upande! \q Mshitakini, nasi tumshitaki!" \q Watu wote wa amani yangu \q wanavizia kujikwaa kwangu: \q "Huenda atashawishika, nasi tutamshinda \q na kulipiza kisasi chetu juu yake."
sw.B: Nasikia wengi wakinong'ona, "Hofu kila upande! \q Mshitakini! Na tumshitaki!" \q Rafiki zangu wote niliowaamini \q wanangoja nijikwae: \q "Huenda atashawishika; ndipo tutamshinda \q na kulipiza kisasi juu yake."
sw.R: Nasikia watu wengi wakinong'ona, "Hofu pande zote! \q Mshitakini! Na tumshitaki!" \q Hata rafiki zangu wa karibu kabisa \q wanangoja niteleze. \q Wanasema, "Huenda atadanganyika. Ndipo tutamshinda \q na kumlipiza."

decisions.choice: Terror on every side: Jeremiah's own saying turned against him
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had used these words of the coming enemy (6:25) and had just made them Pashhur's name (verse 3). Now people repeat them about him in whispers, as a mocking nickname or as the charge against him (compare Psalm 31:14, where the same words stand beside the whispering of many).

decisions.choice: tell, and let us tell on him: report him to the authorities
decisions.reason: The verb means to tell or declare; here it means to inform against someone, to bring a charge. Pashhur's action in verses 1-2 shows what such a report could lead to (compare 26:8-11).

decisions.choice: men of my peace: friends he trusted
decisions.reason: "Man of my peace" means someone with whom one is at peace, a close friend (38:22; Psalm 41:10; Obadiah 7). Even those near him wait for him to fall.

decisions.choice: enticed ... prevail: the words of verse 7 again
decisions.reason: His enemies use the same two verbs Jeremiah used of God in verse 7. They hope he can be lured into a mistake, as God lured him into his calling, so that they can overcome him. Verse 11 answers with the same verb: they will not prevail.

decisions.choice: Even ... They say
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Even" to show that friends are the last people who should do this, and "They say" to mark whose words follow.

decisions.choice: enticed (Literal, Balanced); fooled (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same English words as for the same verb in verse 7, so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: Terror por todas partes (Literal, Balanced); Hay terror por todos lados (Readable)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's own saying, turned against him (meaning decision m1), keeps the Spanish words of verse 3.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֤ה אוֹתִי֙ כְּגִבּ֣וֹר עָרִ֔יץ עַל־כֵּ֛ן רֹדְפַ֥י יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יֻכָ֑לוּ בֹּ֤שׁוּ מְאֹד֙ כִּֽי־לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּ֔ילוּ כְּלִמַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: But Yahweh [is] with me like a warrior dreaded; therefore my pursuers will stumble and not prevail; they will be shamed greatly, for not they have succeeded, [a] disgrace of perpetuity [that] not will be forgotten.

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with me like a fearsome warrior; \q therefore my pursuers will stumble and not prevail. \q They will be greatly put to shame, for they have not succeeded, \q [with] an everlasting disgrace [that] will not be forgotten.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with me like a terrifying warrior; \q so those who hunt me will stumble and will not win. \q They will be thoroughly shamed when they fail, \q with a lasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with me like a strong and terrifying soldier. \q So the people chasing me will trip and fall. They will not win. \q They will fail, and they will be completely shamed. \q People will never forget their disgrace.

es.L: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [está] conmigo como un guerrero temible; \q por tanto, mis perseguidores tropezarán y no prevalecerán. \q Serán avergonzados en gran manera, porque no tuvieron éxito, \q [con] una afrenta eterna [que] no será olvidada.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está conmigo como un guerrero terrible; \q por eso, los que me persiguen tropezarán y no vencerán. \q Quedarán completamente avergonzados al fracasar, \q con una deshonra que durará y nunca se olvidará.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está conmigo como un soldado fuerte y temible. \q Por eso, los que me persiguen tropezarán y caerán. No vencerán. \q Fracasarán y quedarán totalmente avergonzados. \q La gente nunca olvidará su deshonra.

sw.L: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yu] pamoja nami kama shujaa wa kutisha; \q kwa hiyo wanaonifuatia watajikwaa, wala hawatashinda. \q Wataaibishwa sana, kwa maana hawakufanikiwa, \q [kwa] fedheha ya milele isiyosahaulika.
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja nami kama shujaa wa kutisha; \q kwa hiyo wanaoniwinda watajikwaa, wala hawatashinda. \q Wataaibika kabisa watakaposhindwa, \q kwa fedheha ya kudumu isiyosahaulika kamwe.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko pamoja nami kama askari hodari wa kutisha. \q Kwa hiyo wanaonifukuza watajikwaa na kuanguka. Hawatashinda. \q Watashindwa, nao wataaibika kabisa. \q Watu hawatasahau kamwe aibu yao.

decisions.choice: a fearsome warrior: God fights on Jeremiah's side
decisions.reason: The second word usually describes ruthless, terrifying men, the oppressors from whom God promised to rescue Jeremiah (15:21, the same word). Here the one who is terrifying is God himself, and he is with Jeremiah, as he promised at his call (1:8, 19).

decisions.choice: the turn to trust
decisions.reason: As in many psalms of lament, the complaint turns to confidence that God will act (Psalm 22:23-25; 31:20-25). Jeremiah takes up the promise God gave him at his call and again later, that his enemies would fight against him but not prevail (1:19; 15:20).

decisions.choice: they have not succeeded
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to act wisely or to succeed (10:21; 23:5). Here it is their plan that fails; "they have not acted wisely" is also possible.

decisions.choice: not prevail: the answer to verse 10
decisions.reason: His enemies said "we will prevail against him" (verse 10). Jeremiah answers with the same verb: they will not.

decisions.choice: strong and terrifying soldier
decisions.reason: Readable gives the word for a warrior as "strong ... soldier" and splits the long sentence; "their disgrace" says whose shame is meant.

en.L: And {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, testing the righteous, \q seeing kidneys and heart, \q let me see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} vengeance on them, \q for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have revealed my case.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who test the righteous, \q who see the inner feelings and the mind, \q let me see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take vengeance on them, \q for I have laid my case before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} test those who do right. \q You see what people think and feel deep inside. \q Let me see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pay them back for what they have done, \q because I have put my case in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, que pruebas al justo, \q que ves los riñones y el corazón, \q vea yo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} venganza sobre ellos, \q porque a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} he descubierto mi causa.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que pruebas al justo, \q que ves los sentimientos y la mente, \q déjame ver cómo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} te vengas de ellos, \q porque he puesto mi causa delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pruebas a los que hacen lo correcto. \q Ves lo que la gente piensa y siente en lo más profundo. \q Déjame ver cómo les das su merecido, \q porque he puesto mi causa en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos.

sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, unawajaribu wale wanaotenda haki. \q Unaona kile watu wanachowaza na kuhisi ndani kabisa. \q Nikuone ukiwalipa kwa yale waliyoyafanya, \q kwa sababu nimeiweka kesi yangu mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}.

decisions.choice: nearly the same words as 11:20
decisions.reason: Jeremiah repeats his prayer from 11:20, with two differences: there God is the one "judging righteously" and "testing" kidneys and heart; here he is the one "testing the righteous" and "seeing" kidneys and heart. The wording follows 11:20 wherever the Hebrew is the same. Compare 17:10.

decisions.choice: kidneys and heart: the inner feelings and the mind
decisions.reason: The kidneys stand for a person's deepest feelings and the heart for the mind and will. God sees all of a person, inside and out (11:20; 17:10; Psalm 7:10).

decisions.choice: let me see your vengeance: Jeremiah leaves the punishment to God
decisions.reason: He does not take revenge himself, as his enemies plan to do (verse 10). He asks God, the just judge, to act, and to let him see it (Deuteronomy 32:35; Psalm 94:1-2).

decisions.choice: the righteous: the one who is in the right
decisions.reason: Jeremiah means himself, the one who is in the right in this quarrel (compare 12:1). God tests such a person and knows that he is innocent.

decisions.choice: wording of 11:20
decisions.reason: All three levels reuse the wording of 11:20 so the repeated prayer is recognized, changing only what the Hebrew changes. Balanced and Readable leave out the opening "And", which in English would join the cry too loosely to the line before.

decisions.choice: los riñones y el corazón
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pair, the seat of feeling and the seat of thought (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say what they mean.

decisions.choice: figo na moyo
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the kidneys (the inner feelings) and the heart (the mind); Balanced and Readable say what they mean.

records.literal_gloss: Sing to Yahweh! Praise Yahweh! For he has rescued [the] life of [the] needy from [the] hand of evildoers.

en.L: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has snatched the life of the needy one out of the hand of evildoers.
en.B: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rescued the poor from the power of those who do evil.
en.R: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q He has rescued the helpless one from the power of evil people.

sw.L: Mwimbieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Kwa maana ameiokoa nafsi ya mhitaji kutoka mkononi mwa watenda maovu.

sw.R: Mwimbieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Amemwokoa mnyonge kutoka katika nguvu za watu waovu.

decisions.choice: a sudden call to praise in the middle of the lament
decisions.reason: Laments often end in praise (Psalm 22:23-27; 69:31-37). Here the praise stands between the confidence of verses 11-12 and the curse of verses 14-18. It may be the praise Jeremiah knows he will give, or a moment of relief before despair returns; the text does not join the pieces.

decisions.choice: the needy one: a poor and helpless person, here Jeremiah himself
decisions.reason: The word means someone poor and without power to defend himself, whom God hears and rescues (Psalm 69:34; 72:12-13). Jeremiah counts himself as one of them.

decisions.choice: has rescued: a rescue already done, or one as certain as if it were done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for completed action. It can describe a rescue God has already given or one Jeremiah is so sure of that he speaks of it as done.

decisions.choice: power
decisions.reason: The "hand" of evildoers is their power over someone; Balanced and Readable say "power".

source.text: אָר֣וּר הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּ֖דְתִּי בּ֑וֹ י֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יְלָדַ֥תְנִי אִמִּ֖י אַל־יְהִ֥י בָרֽוּךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Cursed [be] the day which I was born on it; [the] day when bore me my mother, let not it be blessed.

en.L: Cursed [be] the day on which I was born! \q The day my mother bore me, let it not be blessed!
en.B: A curse on the day I was born! \q May the day my mother gave birth to me never be blessed!
en.R: May the day I was born be cursed! \q May no one bless the day my mother gave birth to me!

es.L: ¡Maldito [sea] el día en que nací! \q El día en que me dio a luz mi madre, ¡que no sea bendito!
es.B: ¡Maldito el día en que nací! \q ¡Que nunca sea bendecido el día en que mi madre me dio a luz!
es.R: ¡Que sea maldito el día en que nací! \q ¡Que nadie bendiga el día en que mi madre me dio a luz!

sw.L: Imelaaniwa siku ile niliyozaliwa! \q Siku ile mama yangu aliyonizaa, isibarikiwe!
sw.B: Na ilaaniwe siku niliyozaliwa! \q Siku ambayo mama yangu alinizaa isibarikiwe kamwe!
sw.R: Siku niliyozaliwa na ilaaniwe! \q Mtu yeyote asiibariki siku ambayo mama yangu alinizaa!

decisions.choice: cursing the day of his birth, as Job does
decisions.reason: Job opens his complaint by cursing the day he was born (Job 3:1-10; compare 3:3). Jeremiah's words in verses 14-18 are very close to Job's, and both say they wish they had never lived (verse 18; Job 3:11).

decisions.choice: a cry of despair, not a curse on God or his parents
decisions.reason: Jeremiah curses a day that is long past, which can no longer be harmed. He does not curse God (Leviticus 24:15) or his mother and father (Exodus 21:17). The words show how deep his pain is, and the book keeps them without softening them.

decisions.choice: A curse on
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "A curse on" for the short Hebrew "cursed"; Literal keeps "Cursed [be]" and Readable "May ... be cursed".

source.text: אָר֣וּר הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשַּׂ֤ר אֶת־אָבִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻֽלַּד־לְךָ֖ בֵּ֣ן זָכָ֑ר שַׂמֵּ֖חַ שִׂמֳּחָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Cursed [be] the man who brought news [to] my father, saying, Has been born to you a son, a male, making glad, he made him glad.

en.L: Cursed [be] the man who brought the news to my father, saying, \q "A son has been born to you, a male!" \q making him very glad.
en.B: A curse on the man who brought my father the news, \q "You have a son, a boy!" \q and made him so very glad.
en.R: May the man be cursed who brought my father the news, \q "You have a baby boy!" \q That news made my father very happy.

es.L: ¡Maldito [sea] el hombre que dio la noticia a mi padre, diciendo: \q «Te ha nacido un hijo, un varón», \q alegrándolo mucho!
es.B: ¡Maldito el hombre que le dio a mi padre la noticia: \q «¡Tienes un hijo, un varón!», \q y lo llenó de alegría!
es.R: ¡Que sea maldito el hombre que le dio a mi padre la noticia: \q «¡Te ha nacido un niño!». \q Esa noticia hizo muy feliz a mi padre.

sw.L: Amelaaniwa mtu yule aliyemletea baba yangu habari, akisema, \q "Umezaliwa mwana, mtoto wa kiume!" \q akimfurahisha sana.
sw.B: Na alaaniwe mtu aliyemletea baba yangu habari, \q "Umepata mwana, mtoto wa kiume!" \q akamfurahisha mno.
sw.R: Na alaaniwe mtu aliyemletea baba yangu habari, \q "Umepata mtoto wa kiume!" \q Habari hiyo ilimfurahisha baba yangu sana.

decisions.choice: the man who brought the news: the messenger of a birth
decisions.reason: The father was not present at the birth, and someone brought him word. Such good news was welcomed and often rewarded (compare 2 Samuel 4:10; 18:19-27). The birth of a son, who would carry on the family, brought special joy.

decisions.choice: a son, a male ... making glad, he made him glad
decisions.reason: The news names the child twice, a son and a male, for emphasis, and the verb "made glad" is doubled to say how great the father's joy was. The joy of that day is set against Jeremiah's misery now.

decisions.choice: the messenger is cursed in place of the parents
decisions.reason: By cursing the man who brought the news, Jeremiah curses his birth without cursing his father or mother, which the law forbade (Exodus 21:17).

decisions.choice: a son, a boy (Balanced); a baby boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the doubled naming with "a son, a boy"; Readable joins the two words. Readable also makes the last line a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: the cities the LORD overthrew: Sodom and Gomorrah
decisions.reason: "Overthrew" is the word used for the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities near them (Genesis 19:25; Deuteronomy 29:22; Jeremiah 49:18; Amos 4:11). Those cities became the picture of complete and final ruin.

decisions.choice: did not relent: did not change his mind or hold back
decisions.reason: The verb means to be sorry, to change one's mind, or to have compassion. God sometimes turns back from a disaster he has announced (18:8), but not in the case of those cities.

decisions.choice: a cry ... a battle shout: the sounds of a city under attack
decisions.reason: The first word is a cry for help; the second is the shout or trumpet blast that signals war (4:19; 49:2). He wishes on the man the terror of attack, from morning until noon.

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 17
decisions.reason: Verse 17 gives the reason for the curse, so this record ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: destroyed without mercy
decisions.reason: Readable says "destroyed" for "overthrew" and "without mercy" for "did not relent", the plain sense of both.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־מוֹתְתַ֖נִי מֵרָ֑חֶם וַתְּהִי־לִ֤י אִמִּי֙ קִבְרִ֔י וְרַחְמָ֖הֿ הֲרַ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: because not he killed me from [the] womb, and would have been to me my mother my grave, and her womb pregnant [of] perpetuity.

en.L: because he did not kill me from the womb, \q so that my mother would have been my grave, \q and her womb pregnant forever.
en.B: because he did not kill me in the womb; \q then my mother would have been my grave, \q her womb pregnant for all time.
en.R: because he did not kill me before I was born. \q Then my mother's body would have been my grave, \q and she would have stayed pregnant with me forever.

es.L: porque no me mató desde el vientre, \q para que mi madre hubiera sido mi sepulcro, \q y su vientre preñado para siempre.
es.B: porque no me mató en el vientre; \q así mi madre habría sido mi tumba, \q y su vientre habría quedado encinta para siempre.
es.R: porque no me mató antes de nacer. \q Entonces el vientre de mi madre habría sido mi tumba, \q y ella se habría quedado embarazada de mí para siempre.

sw.L: kwa sababu hakuniua tangu tumboni, \q ili mama yangu angekuwa kaburi langu, \q na tumbo lake lingebaki na mimba milele.
sw.B: kwa sababu hakuniua nikiwa tumboni; \q ndipo mama yangu angekuwa kaburi langu, \q tumbo lake likiwa na mimba milele.
sw.R: kwa sababu hakuniua kabla sijazaliwa. \q Ndipo tumbo la mama yangu lingekuwa kaburi langu, \q naye angebaki na mimba yangu milele.

decisions.choice: he did not kill me: the man who brought the news
alternatives: it (the day) did not kill me
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject named. The nearest is the man of verses 15-16, who is cursed for not ending Jeremiah's life before birth. The line is the bitter, unreasonable logic of grief, not a real charge against the man. Some read it as impersonal ("one did not kill me"), or as speaking of the day or of God.

decisions.choice: dying before birth, as Job wished
decisions.reason: Job also wished that he had died in the womb or been stillborn (Job 3:10-11, 16; 10:18-19).

decisions.choice: my mother my grave, her womb pregnant forever
decisions.reason: The picture is of a child who never leaves the womb, so that the womb becomes his tomb. It is the strongest way of saying he wishes he had never come into the world.

decisions.choice: in the womb / before I was born
decisions.reason: "From the womb" means at or before birth; Balanced says "in the womb" and Readable "before I was born".

source.text: לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ מֵרֶ֣חֶם יָצָ֔אתִי לִרְא֥וֹת עָמָ֖ל וְיָג֑וֹן וַיִּכְל֥וּ בְּבֹ֖שֶׁת יָמָֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Why this from [the] womb did I come out, to see trouble and sorrow, and have come to an end in shame my days?

en.L: Why is it that I came out from the womb \q to see trouble and sorrow, \q and my days have come to an end in shame?
en.B: Why did I ever come out of the womb \q to look on hardship and grief, \q and to have my days run out in shame?
en.R: Why was I ever born? \q Was it to see trouble and sorrow, \q and to end my life in shame?

es.L: ¿Por qué salí del vientre \q para ver trabajo y dolor, \q y que mis días se acaben en vergüenza?
es.B: ¿Por qué salí del vientre \q para ver penas y aflicción, \q y para que mis días terminen en vergüenza?
es.R: ¿Por qué tuve que nacer? \q ¿Fue para ver sufrimiento y tristeza, \q y para terminar mi vida en vergüenza?

sw.L: Mbona nilitoka tumboni \q ili kuona taabu na huzuni, \q na siku zangu zimalizike katika aibu?
sw.B: Kwa nini nilitoka tumboni kamwe \q ili nione taabu na majonzi, \q na siku zangu zimalizike katika aibu?
sw.R: Kwa nini nilizaliwa? \q Je, ni ili nione taabu na huzuni, \q na kumaliza maisha yangu katika aibu?

decisions.choice: why was I born: the question Job asks
decisions.reason: Job asks the same question (Job 3:11, 20; 10:18). Jeremiah ends his prayer with it.

decisions.choice: trouble and sorrow: hard toil and grief
decisions.reason: The first word means painful labor and the trouble that comes with it; the second is grief or sorrow of heart. They sum up his life as a prophet.

decisions.choice: the lament ends without an answer
decisions.reason: The prayer closes in shame and with a question, and no reply from God follows, as one does after 12:1-4 and 15:15-18. The book leaves the question standing; the next chapter goes on with Jeremiah still at work as God's prophet (21:1-2).

decisions.choice: why this: an emphatic "why"
decisions.reason: "Why this" strengthens the question: why ever, for what possible reason.

decisions.choice: Why was I ever born? Was it to see ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the one long question into two shorter ones, keeping its meaning.
